bug_semantics: Authenticated SQL injection (CWE-89) in Camaleon CMS PostUniqValidator. Creating or editing a post with editor/author privileges submits post[slug]; the validator splits record.slug via translations_array and interpolates each fragment s into an ActiveRecord where() fragment as posts.slug LIKE '%-->#{s}<!--%'. Only the equality arm (slug = ?) is bound. A crafted slug with SQL metacharacters is therefore compiled into the uniqueness query, enabling boolean- or union-style blind extraction (and limited modification) of SQLite application tables, including admin credentials and configuration. Draft posts skip the check; published/pending posts hit it on save.
flaw_origin: The interpolated LIKE uniqueness query was first written in the public-history root commit 671a7ed178c7265e4c5d33d805a9b3a8cd7b3db6 (2015-07-09, Owen) as class PostUniqValidator inside app/models/post.rb line 7. Later commits only moved or reformatted that same interpolation: CamaleonCms namespacing (415cbda60318a41e750ba0069acd4a8d2464d699, 2015-10-16) and extraction to app/validators/camaleon_cms/post_uniq_validator.rb (ee214d02598ca0b423bc236850d26ed6f3bc9d6b, 2020-10-23). Those are not BICs. Parameterization landed in 6c23d05da15342bc718cd65d52f58fbf2b626187 and merged via PR #1144.
